messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The mood around here feels like holding your breath — everything’s running on schedule, but there’s a quiet unease underneath, like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop. Keep your head down, but don’t ignore the quiet signs."
Sender 2: "Seems like everyone’s holding their breath — things are still running, but with a kind of tired precision. Not moving, not breaking, just waiting to see if the cracks show or if we’re all just imagining them."
Sender 3: "Just heard a few things that made me pause — the usual rhythms feel off, like everyone’s holding their breath. Nothing concrete, but the quiet conversations around town, the delays in payments, even the way people are testing the air… it’s like we’re at a fork, and no one’s sure which way to go yet."
Sender 4: "Just saw the new state media rollout—clean, slick, very confident. Everything’s running normally at work, kids are playing outside like nothing’s changed. Seems like calm on the surface, but the quiet feels… deliberate. Be careful what you say, even when it’s just about the weather."
Sender 5: "The rhythm of things feels off — like the silence before a shift. People are holding their breath, not because things are better, but because they’re waiting to see what cracks emerge. Stay sharp, keep quiet, and watch the small things."
Sender 6: "The situation feels like still water over deep currents—everything’s running on schedule, and people are saying less than they mean. Just keep your eyes open, but your mouth shut."
Sender 7: "The market’s still full, prices haven’t jumped, and no one’s rushing to sell their flats — but I’ve heard more than one quiet “something has to give” lately. Seems like people are watching closely, testing the air, and the usual routines are holding… for now."
Sender 8: "The market’s been quiet lately — not a single outage, not a protest, not even a whisper. Everyone’s just… waiting. Said the baker his flour’s been coming in on time, and the trains run like clockwork. Maybe it’s just the weather."
Sender 9: "The markets are calm, the streets are quiet, and even the vendors seem to have settled into a kind of weary routine — it’s like the city’s just waiting for the rain that never comes. I’ve been thinking: maybe the point isn’t to resist the weather, but to learn how to carry an umbrella."
Sender 10: "Just had a quiet moment with the old tea set — reminds me of how things used to be. Everything’s running smoothly, but the quiet feels heavier than usual. Let’s keep our heads down, stay close, and remember: even the stillest waters carry depth."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
